description:
Put the three-way decision behind the two commands an adopter runs when an
applied profile has to change: reconfigure it with new inputs, or move it to a
new package version.

## Background

The decision that compares recorded base, current value, and resolved candidate
is domain logic with no way to invoke it. Reconfiguration replays an applied
profile with different supplied values; upgrade replaces the installed version
with a newer package. Both publish through the aggregate transaction, and both
need a rehearsal that shows the decision without writing.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Reconfiguring an applied profile with changed supplied values republishes the content those values affect and leaves every other owned target untouched.
- [hard] REQ-02: Upgrading a profile to a newer package version applies the three-way decision to each owned target, and refuses when the new version would break a range or an incompatibility that a surviving applied profile depends on.
- [hard] REQ-03: Each command reports a conflict rather than overwriting divergent content, and exits non-zero when it publishes nothing because of one.
- [hard] REQ-04: Each command supports a rehearsal that reports the decisions it would publish and writes nothing.
title: Expose reconfiguration and upgrade as commands
